title: Foundations
goal: Basic facts about operators, states, energy and ground energy that every later argument uses.
wanted: Lemmas that a later program visibly needs. Not restatements of Mathlib, and not variations of lemmas already in the record.

title: Locality and tensor structure
goal: How operators on different sets of qubits or qudits combine: products, commutation, supports, and operators built from smaller ones.
wanted: Closure properties of QActsOn, embedding an operator on few qudits into many, and how energy behaves for operators on disjoint supports.

title: Classical constraint problems as Hamiltonians
goal: The bridge to the classical PCP theorem: a constraint satisfaction problem is a diagonal normalized Hamiltonian whose ground energy counts violated constraints.
wanted: Sums of diagonal terms, ground energy as the minimum number of violated constraints, and classical instances as RelYes and RelNo instances.

title: Manipulating the promise gap
goal: Operations on normalized Hamiltonians that preserve or change the relative gap in a controlled way: rescaling, padding with trivial terms, repeating terms, and changing locality bounds.
wanted: For each operation, a lemma giving the new term count and bounds on the new ground energy in terms of the old.

title: Commuting and frustration-free Hamiltonians
goal: Hamiltonians whose terms commute, or whose ground energy is zero: the simplest quantum instances, and the setting of the known special cases of the conjecture.
wanted: Definitions are not open to contributors yet, so state lemmas directly in terms of Commute and groundEnergyOn.

title: A formal statement of the conjecture
goal: Define quantum verification (QMA), reductions, and the promise problem, and state the quantum PCP conjecture in Lean.
wanted: Closed to proposals. This needs new definitions, which must be written and reviewed by a specialist in Hamiltonian complexity.

title: Known theorems
goal: Formalize established results around the conjecture, such as QMA-completeness of the local Hamiltonian problem and the NLTS theorem.
wanted: Closed until the statement program has the definitions these theorems are about.
